content: The following studies provide insights into tuberculosis (TB) transmission, diagnosis, and prevention strategies across various global settings: 1. A study in Alexandria, Egypt, explored pulmonary tuberculosis cases, contributing to the understanding of TB epidemiology in the region (J Egypt Public Health Assoc, 2012). 2. Research in northern Iran examined the prevalence of latent TB infection and smear-positive pulmonary TB among individuals in close household contact with TB patients, highlighting the risks of transmission within families (Iranian Journal of Medical Sciences, 2015). 3. 4. A Japanese study investigated the association between low sputum smear positivity in TB patients and IGRA outcomes among close contacts, emphasizing the role of diagnostic tools in contact tracing (Int J Environ Res Public Health, 2019). 5. In the United States, risk factors for TB transmission among African Americans and Whites were analyzed, providing insights into demographic disparities in TB spread (Int J Tuberc Lung Dis, 2015). 6. A study in Western Sydney, Australia, monitored TB contact tracing outcomes, offering data on the effectiveness of public health interventions in urban settings (BMJ Open Respir Res, 2018). 7. Research in Spain assessed the long-term risk of active TB among household index cases, emphasizing the importance of sustained follow-up in TB prevention (Public Health Nurs, 2017). 8. A U.S.-based study identified risk factors for TB and evaluated the impact of preventive therapy among close contacts of infectious TB patients, underscoring the benefits of early intervention (Clin Infect Dis, 2019). 9. A 21-year retrospective cohort study in the UK identified predictors of contact tracing completion and outcomes, providing valuable data for improving TB control programs (Int J Tuberc Lung Dis, 2014). 10. In Amsterdam, a 10-year follow-up study of TB contacts revealed opportunities for enhancing contact investigation strategies to reduce TB incidence (Am J Respir Crit Care Med, 2014). 11. A study in Cambodia demonstrated the effectiveness of community-based active case finding for early TB detection, particularly in high-burden settings (BMC Public Health, 2012). 12. Research in Rwanda found that the Xpert MTB/RIF assay did not significantly improve TB diagnosis among child contacts, highlighting the need for alternative diagnostic approaches (Pan Afr Med J, 2018). 13. A study in Ethiopia evaluated the utility of contact investigation for detecting latent and active TB cases, emphasizing its role in TB control efforts (PLoS One, 2014). 14. In Southern China, the impact of socioeconomic status and Mycobacterium tuberculosis genotypes on household TB transmission was analyzed, providing insights into localized transmission dynamics (Int J Environ Res Public Health, 2019). 15. A study in India highlighted the significance of family surveys for detecting TB cases among household contacts, demonstrating the value of targeted screening (Indian Pediatr, 2011). 16. Research in Brazil examined the correlation between tuberculin skin tests and IGRAs with risk factors for TB spread among close contacts, offering data on diagnostic accuracy (BMC Infect Dis, 2014). 17. A study in Uganda assessed the feasibility and yield of household child TB contact screening, emphasizing the importance of early detection in pediatric populations (Int J Tuberc Lung Dis, 2017). 18. In South Africa, the use of Xpert MTB/RIF for active case finding among TB contacts was evaluated, demonstrating its potential to enhance TB diagnosis in high-burden areas (Tuberc Res Treat, 2016). 19. 20. Research in Vietnam explored active contact tracing beyond households for multidrug-resistant TB, providing evidence for expanding contact investigation strategies (BMC Public Health, 2019). These studies collectively underscore the importance of contact tracing, diagnostic advancements, and preventive strategies in controlling TB transmission and improving outcomes for affected populations.
